title: CVE-2026-8932: incomplete mTLS config matching in conn reuse
excerpt:
Hi all,

This report (and my multiple subsequent ones) may come as a surprise, as I was assured that curl now had zero vulnerabilities in it.

Nonetheless, I think the CVE-2022-27782 fix ("TLS and SSH connection too eager reuse", commit `f18af4f874` 2022-05-09, "tls: check more TLS details for connection reuse") was incomplete: it moved a batch of SSL knobs into `ssl_primary_config` so conn-reuse would compare them, but left the credential-half of the mTLS pair behind in `ssl_config_data`. Two easy handles sharing a `CURLSH`/`CURLM` pool can reuse each other's authenticated TLS connection whenever they differ only on `SSLKEY`, `SSLKEY_BLOB`, `KEYPASSWD`, `SSLKEYTYPE`, or `SSLCERTTYPE`. The second handle silently inherits the first's authenticated identity to the server.

The conn-reuse gate is `match_ssl_primary_config` at `lib/vtls/vtls.c:194-225`, called via `Curl_ssl_conn_config_match` (`lib/vtls/vtls.c:227-240`) from `url_match_ssl_config` in `lib/url.c:991-1003`. Its argument type is `struct ssl_primary_config *` — it literally cannot see anything outside primary. The struct split is in `lib/urldata.h:143-168` (primary, compared) vs `lib/urldata.h:170-193` (`ssl_config_data`, not compared). `connectdata` (`lib/urldata.h:389-392`) only carries the primary copy into the pool, so once a conn is parked the full `ssl_config_data` it was born from is gone.

A similar gap exists in the TLS session cache. `Curl_ssl_peer_key_make` (`lib/vtls/vtls_scache.c:137-294`) builds the scache lookup key from primary only, and for the client cert it just adds a literal `:CCERT` marker — same five bytes regardless of which key/cert is set:

```c
if(ssl->clientcert && ssl->clientcert[0]) {
  r = curlx_dyn_add(&buf, ":CCERT");
```

The secondary auth-match check at `lib/vtls/vtls_scache.c:607-627` (`cf_ssl_scache_match_auth`) compares only `clientcert` and SRP creds — never key, key blob, key passwd, key type, or cert type. (Caveat: in practice the wrong-passwd case eagerly fails inside `client_cert()` before session-resume can hide it, so the scache gap is real-but-narrow for the passphrase variant specifically. The key-blob / key-type variants don't have that eager-fail.)

PoC: two easy handles attached to a `CURLSH` with `CURL_LOCK_DATA_CONNECT` + `CURL_LOCK_DATA_SSL_SESSION`. Both target `https://server.test:8443/`, both set the same `SSLCERT=clientA.crt` / `SSLKEY=client

summary: A second curl handle with wrong mTLS credentials silently reuses an existing TLS connection authenticated with a different client identity, allowing impersonation within the same process.

claims.reasoning: The PoC's observed behavior matches the code path: standalone fails at key load; shared pool reuses connection and skips key load entirely.

key_reasons: The struct split (ssl_primary_config vs ssl_config_data) is real and grounded in lib/urldata.h. Credential fields (key_passwd, key, key_blob, key_type, cert_type) exist only in ssl_config_data and are never compared during connection reuse or session cache lookup.

match_ssl_primary_config (lib/vtls/vtls.c:194-225) and cf_ssl_scache_match_auth (lib/vtls/vtls_scache.c:607-627) both omit these fields. connectdata (lib/urldata.h:389) stores only primary config, discarding the credential half when a connection is parked.

The PoC demonstrates a concrete attack: two handles sharing a CURLSH pool with CURL_LOCK_DATA_CONNECT + CURL_LOCK_DATA_SSL_SESSION; handle A authenticates with correct KEYPASSWD, handle B (wrong KEYPASSWD) reuses A's connection and inherits A's client identity. Server sees CN=alice for both requests on the same connection ID.

This is the same class of flaw as CVE-2022-27782 (incomplete TLS config comparison for connection reuse). It enables silent credential confusion/impersonation in mTLS scenarios where client cert identity maps to authorization — a clear security impact.
Master (db4a6f286bbc) still has the gap; the fix proposed by the reporter (promote fields into primary, extend match functions and scache key) is the correct shape.
reply: Thanks for the detailed report and PoC. The claims are grounded: ssl_primary_config omits key_passwd, key, key_blob, key_type, cert_type; match_ssl_primary_config and cf_ssl_scache_match_auth don't compare them; connectdata stores only primary. The PoC shows a real mTLS credential-confusion bug — handle B with a wrong passphrase reuses handle A's authenticated connection. This is a valid security issue (same class as CVE-2022-27782). We'll promote the missing fields into primary and extend the match/scache logic as you outlined.
